title: Principal supported-section quotients of powerwise injective sequences
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $a\in R$, and let $0\to N_1\xrightarrow{i}N_2\xrightarrow{j}N_3\to0$ be a short exact sequence of $R$-modules [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. Suppose $N_1/a^nN_1\to N_2/a^nN_2$ is injective for every $n\geq0$. Put $T_k=\Gamma_{(a)}(N_k)=\{x\in N_k:\exists n\geq0,\ a^nx=0\}$ [def-nagata-power-torsion, lemma-nagata-power-torsion-submodule]. Write $Z=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $h:D(a)\hookrightarrow Z$ for the principal open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], and $\widetilde N_k$ for the associated module sheaves [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]. Define $K_k\subseteq\widetilde N_k$ on each open $W\subseteq Z$ by $K_k(W)=\ker(\widetilde N_k(W)\to\widetilde N_k(W\cap D(a)))$ and put $Q_k=\widetilde N_k/K_k$, the quotient in module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then:

(1) On every principal open $D(s)\subseteq Z$, the kernel $K_k(D(s))\subseteq(N_k)_s$ is $\Gamma_{(a/1)}((N_k)_s)$ and is precisely the image of the injective localization map $(T_k)_s\to(N_k)_s$. These identifications commute with restriction and are natural for $R$-linear maps. In particular $K_k=\widetilde T_k$ as submodules of $\widetilde N_k$, and there are natural isomorphisms $Q_k\cong\widetilde{N_k/T_k}$, compatible with the maps from $\widetilde N_k$ [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module].

(2) The maps $i,j$ induce a short exact sequence $0\to N_1/T_1\xrightarrow{\bar i}N_2/T_2\xrightarrow{\bar j}N_3/T_3\to0$, with $\bar i([y])=[i(y)]$ and $\bar j([x])=[j(x)]$. Associated sheafification takes this sequence to a short exact sequence, and the isomorphisms in (1) identify it, including the maps induced from $\widetilde i,\widetilde j$, with $0\to Q_1\to Q_2\to Q_3\to0$. No non-zero-divisor condition on $a$ or finiteness hypothesis on the modules is required.

proof.text: Use the associated-sheaf functor of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction]. Its component on $D(s)$ for an $R$-linear map $f:M\to N$ is $m/s^r\mapsto f(m)/s^r$: the global component sends $m$ to $f(m)$, restriction gives the same equality on constant sections, and $R_s$-linearity gives the formula on every fraction, using [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]. In particular the functor preserves zero maps and sums. By [lem-sc-tilde-preserves-finite-limits] it preserves the zero object and kernels; by clause (4) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] it preserves cokernels, which are finite colimits. Thus it carries a short exact module sequence to a short exact sequence of module sheaves: the first arrow remains the kernel of the second, and the second remains the cokernel of the first. Here kernels and cokernels are those of the abelian module-sheaf category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. This argument uses arbitrary modules over any commutative ring.

proof.text: Fix one $N=N_k$ and put $T=\Gamma_{(a)}(N)$. On $D(s)$ the restriction defining $K$ is $N_s\to N_{sa}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]. Inverting $a/1$ in $N_s$ gives $N_{sa}$: the maps are induced by $x/s^r\mapsto x/s^r$ and satisfy the localization universal property, since inverting $sa$ makes both $s$ and $a$ invertible and conversely. Hence [lemma-nagata-power-torsion-kernel-localization], applied over $R_s$, identifies this kernel with $\Gamma_{(a/1)}(N_s)$. By [lemma-nagata-power-torsion-localization] that submodule is the localized image of $T$. The map $T_s\to N_s$ is injective by [lem-sc-p1-localization-short-exact] applied to $0\to T\to N\to N/T\to0$. Step 1 makes $\widetilde T\to\widetilde N$ a monomorphism; its basis components are exactly these maps, so its image subsheaf and $K$ agree on every $D(s)$. Principal opens are a basis directly from the Zariski topology: the complement of $V(I)$ is $\bigcup_{s\in I}D(s)$. The sheaf property therefore gives equality on every open (equivalently apply [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-morphism-on-basis]). All identifications respect restriction: they identify submodules using the same restriction map of $\widetilde N$. They are natural for $f:N\to N'$ because $a^nx=0$ implies $a^nf(x)=0$ and the fraction formula of Step 1 commutes with localization. This proves the kernel and naturality assertions of (1).

proof.text: Let $\pi_N:N\to N/T$ be the quotient map [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module]. Apply Step 1 to $0\to T\to N\xrightarrow{\pi_N}N/T\to0$. By Step 2 its sheafified first term is the submodule $K$. Thus $\widetilde{\pi_N}$ has kernel $K$ and is its cokernel quotient. The definition of $Q=\widetilde N/K$ in the module-sheaf category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] gives a unique isomorphism $\theta_N:Q\to\widetilde{N/T}$ satisfying $\theta_N\circ q_N=\widetilde{\pi_N}$, where $q_N:\widetilde N\to Q$. For any linear $f:N\to N'$ the induced maps preserve $T$ and $K$ by Step 2. Both composites in the naturality square for $\theta$ become $\widetilde{\pi_{N'}f}$ after precomposition with the epimorphism $q_N$, so they agree. This proves the natural quotient isomorphisms and compatibility with the original maps in (1).

source.place: definition-strict-transform (1); elementary cokernel assembly using Schemes Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves

proof.text: Every linear map sends power torsion into power torsion: if $a^nx=0$ then $a^nf(x)=0$ [def-nagata-power-torsion]. It therefore induces the displayed coset maps on the quotient modules [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module]. Their composite is zero since $ji=0$. If $\bar i([y])=0$, then $a^ni(y)=0$ for some $n$, and injectivity of $i$ implies $a^ny=0$, hence $[y]=0$. Thus $\bar i$ is injective. Given $[z]\in N_3/T_3$, surjectivity of $j$ provides $x\in N_2$ with $j(x)=z$, so $\bar j([x])=[z]$. The endpoint hypotheses here are precisely those of the given short exact sequence [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]; no powerwise assumption has yet been used.

source.place: Tag 080W, lemma-strict-transform-universally-injective, algebra paragraph: endpoint injectivity and surjectivity

proof.text: For middle exactness take $[x]\in N_2/T_2$ with $j(x)\in T_3$. Choose $n\geq0$ with $a^nj(x)=0$ [def-nagata-power-torsion]. Exactness of the original sequence gives $y\in N_1$ with $i(y)=a^nx$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. The class of $i(y)$ in $N_2/a^nN_2$ is zero. By the assumed injectivity of $N_1/a^nN_1\to N_2/a^nN_2$, the class of $y$ is zero, so $y=a^nz$ for some $z\in N_1$. Consequently $a^n(x-i(z))=a^nx-i(a^nz)=i(y)-i(y)=0$. Thus $x-i(z)\in T_2$ and $[x]=[i(z)]=\bar i([z])$ [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module]. Together with Step 4 this proves the short exact sequence in (2). This also covers $n=0$, for then $y=z$ and $x=i(z)$. In the last two sentences of the printed Stacks proof the element to subtract and map to $[x]$ is $z$, not $y$; the displayed calculation above corrects that variable error.

source.place: Tag 080W, lemma-strict-transform-universally-injective, final algebra paragraph, with its final variable error corrected

proof.text: Apply the exact functor established in Step 1 to the short exact sequence of Steps 4--5; its exactness is supplied by [lem-sc-tilde-preserves-finite-limits] and clause (4) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction]. Use the isomorphisms $\theta_{N_k}$ of Step 3. Their naturality square for $i$ reads $\theta_{N_2}\circ Q(i)=\widetilde{\bar i}\circ\theta_{N_1}$, and the square for $j$ reads $\theta_{N_3}\circ Q(j)=\widetilde{\bar j}\circ\theta_{N_2}$. These are exactly the maps induced from $\widetilde i,\widetilde j$ because their composites with the respective quotient maps are $q_{N_2}\widetilde i$ and $q_{N_3}\widetilde j$. Hence the resulting short exact sequence is $0\to Q_1\to Q_2\to Q_3\to0$, with the requested maps. No step divided by $a$ inside $R$ or used any finiteness condition; localization and all quotient constructions also allow the zero ring.

lean.statement: theorem principalSupportQuotient_exact (a : R) {N₁ N₂ N₃ : ModuleCat.{u} R} (i : N₁ ⟶ N₂) (j : N₂ ⟶ N₃) (hi : Function.Injective i) (hij : Function.Exact i j) (hj : Function.Surjective j) (hpow : ∀ n : ℕ, Function.Injective (QuotSMulTop.map (a ^ n) i.hom)) : Function.Injective (principalTorsionQuotientMap a i) ∧ Function.Exact (principalTorsionQuotientMap a i) (principalTorsionQuotientMap a j) ∧ Function.Surjective (principalTorsionQuotientMap a j) ∧ (∀ y : N₁, principalTorsionQuotientMap a i (Submodule.Quotient.mk y) = Submodule.Quotient.mk (i y)) ∧ (∀ x : N₂, principalTorsionQuotientMap a j (Submodule.Quotient.mk x) = Submodule.Quotient.mk (j x)) ∧ (∃ h : tilde.map (principalTorsionQuotientMap a i) ≫ tilde.map (principalTorsionQuotientMap a j) = 0, (ShortComplex.mk (tilde.map (principalTorsionQuotientMap a i)) (tilde.map (principalTorsionQuotientMap a j)) h).ShortExact) ∧ (∃ h : principalSupportQuotientMap a i ≫ principalSupportQuotientMap a j = 0, (ShortComplex.mk (principalSupportQuotientMap a i) (principalSupportQuotientMap a j) h).ShortExact)
